title: Reconstruction of Function Fields from Mod-ℓ Milnor K-Theory

issues.location: Sec. 3, Theorem 3.1 (Pop's residual density input) and Lemma 3.2
issues.description: The recognition of residual curves whose constants are algebraic over a finite field (Prop. 3.6) depends on a cited consequence of Pop 2015 (Thm 1.2 and the proof of Thm 4.2, plus the appendix for residue characteristic ℓ). The paper checks the hypotheses it needs (no ℓ-divisible convex subgroup, the auxiliary field κ1), but the cited statement itself could not be checked against the source. This is a dependency risk, not an identified error.
issues.evidence: Theorem 3.1 is stated as 'the consequence of [Pop2015, Theorem 1.2 and the proof of Theorem 4.2, p. 351, item 2]'. The direction of Prop. 3.6 that says 'constants not algebraic over a finite field' needs I_u ⊂ J_v for a constant-reduction quasi-divisor u.

issues.description: Cor. 2.9 applies the local theory to residue fields that may have characteristic ℓ. The paper asserts that Topaz 2020 covers this case with Z/ℓ coefficients. That claim is plausible because the theory is purely multiplicative, but it was not checked against the source.
issues.evidence: 'We state it for finite coefficients; the field in this statement need not have characteristic different from ℓ.'

coverage: Read all of sections 1–8 in full and checked the main proof chain step by step. Section 2: Abhyankar-type inequality, residue duality, approximation, the alternating dimension bound s, the inertia-intersection criterion for quasi-divisors, flag uniqueness via ℓΓ. Section 3: the valuative closed union, the mod-ℓ reduction of the density input, the point-order kernel (Pic^0 is ℓ-divisible), the finite-field test. Section 4: the Bertini integrality argument, independence of the genus bound G_X from the functions, the specialization and the realization by a valuation (no cardinality condition), the five-fiber Riemann–Hurwitz bound (coefficient 5(1−1/ℓ)−2 = 1/2 > 0 at ℓ=2), the char-0 anchor trick that forces residue characteristic ≠ ℓ. Section 5: the Kummer kernel, Hilbert 90 constant descent, finite-dimensional intersection of curve subfields, the incidence lemma (density after removing finitely many points, passage to a fixed curve T′ via normalization and normality of Y~), Aut-invariance of P_N, the exact descent M·P̄0 = L·P̄_L, separability of L/P_L. Section 6: the true-divisor test, good-subfield recognition, good functions as ratios of parameters, the common partner. Section 7: simultaneous values (centers on relation varieties), the purely inseparable transported addition, the PGL2 argument (no semisimple element, unipotent centralizer, χ a field embedding, surjectivity via h), the relation-variety homeomorphism, the field isomorphism. Section 8: separation of divisors via CRT, the global scalar, Frobenius uniqueness. Cited external theorems (Pop 2015, Topaz 2020, Stacks) were taken as stated.
main_claim: For finitely generated K/k and L/l over algebraically closed fields of characteristic ≠ ℓ with trdeg ≥ 2, the map from field isomorphisms of perfect closures that respect constants (modulo Frobenius) to compatible isomorphisms V_K → V_L (K1/ℓ with the Milnor product relations), taken modulo F_ℓ^×, is a bijection.
sibling_notes: This paper shares the pencil-bound, residual-test and incidence architecture of the-Bogomolov-Pop-reconstruction-theorem paper (rank 188, also no_gap_found). The residual risk is the same: the cited Pop 2015 density / residual-curve results. Here the bound is a 5-fiber Riemann–Hurwitz estimate on residual curves of genus ≤ G_X, and curve subfields are obtained by exact descent using M = L·P0.
